classification.habitat: Gardens, sacred groves, cultivated areas and warm open habitats
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated and distributed throughout India

identification.description: Aromatic, erect, much-branched herb with opposite aromatic leaves and terminal flowering spikes.
identification.whole_plant: Erect, aromatic, much-branched herb, commonly 30–60 cm tall.
identification.stem: Erect, branched, hairy and sub-quadrangular stem, often green to purplish.
identification.leaf: Opposite, ovate to elliptic leaves, aromatic and pubescent, with serrate or variable margins.
identification.flower: Small flowers arranged in elongated terminal racemes/spikes, commonly white to purplish depending on form.
identification.fruit: Small dry nutlets enclosed within the persistent calyx.
identification.bark: Not a distinct crude-drug part; stem is herbaceous and becomes firmer with age.

dosha.pitta: may be aggravated in excess because of Ushna-Tikshna profile

therapeutics.dose: API whole-plant monograph: 1–3 g powder. Preparation-specific doses should be taken from the relevant authoritative formulation.
therapeutics.precautions: The heating and sharp qualities warrant preparation- and patient-specific use; verify dosing from an authoritative monograph or formulation.

shlokas:
तुलसी सुरसा ग्राम्या सुलभा बहुमञ्जरी ।
अपेतराक्षसी गौरी भूतघ्नी देवदुन्दुभिः ॥५०॥

तुलसी कटुका तिक्ता हृद्योष्णा दाहपित्तकृत् ।
दीपनी कुष्ठकृच्छ्रास्रपार्श्वरुक्कफवातजित् ।
शुक्ला कृष्णा च तुलसी गुणैस्तुल्या प्रकीर्तिता ॥५१॥

modern_information.evidence_summary: Ocimum tenuiflorum is widely studied for phytochemical and pharmacological properties, particularly its volatile oils and phenolic constituents. Modern findings are not treated here as proof of efficacy for individual diseases.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use preparation-specific dosing and consider potential interactions in patients taking medicines.

exam_points: Botanical name: Ocimum tenuiflorum L. (syn. O. sanctum)
Rasa: Katu-Tikta-Kashaya; Guna: Tikshna-Ruksha-Laghu; Virya: Ushna; Vipaka: Katu
Important actions include Kaphahara, Vatahara, Deepana and Krimighna
viva_questions: State the botanical name and family of Tulasi.
Which part is used in the API Tulasī Pañcāṅga monograph?
mnemonics: Tulasi = aromatic Lamiaceae + opposite leaves + terminal spikes
student.quick_revision: Tulasi (Ocimum tenuiflorum): aromatic Lamiaceae herb; whole plant is official in the API monograph; Ushna, Katu-vipaka and Kaphahara-Vatahara profile.

teaching_points: Demonstrate the characteristic Lamiaceae stem and opposite leaves.
Compare green and purple forms without treating them as separate species without evidence.
discussion_points: Classical Tulasi actions versus modern phytochemical evidence
practical_points: Observe aroma, opposite leaves, hairy quadrangular stem and terminal spikes.

doctor.quick_reference: Tulasi whole plant is an official API monograph drug and is traditionally used in respiratory, digestive and Krimi-related contexts.
doctor.dose: 1–3 g powder according to the API monograph; verify formulation-specific dosing.
key_precautions: Consider heating/sharp qualities and medicine interactions
